history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a CHRISTIAN church entry for Yangkhullen village (Ze Village) in Senapati district — no Hindu temple of this name exists. No congregation specifically named 'Yangkhullen Village Church' is documented online: the village's Christian life is described only in general terms (a travel vlog notes both Roman Catholic and Baptist churches in the village alongside the traditional Heraka faith; IANS reports about 386 of 450 Zeme households are Christian). The entry is therefore documented as the village church(es) of Yangkhullen, denomination uncertain — verify locally which congregation the CSV intends (Baptist vs Catholic). Yangkhullen is the famous 'hanging village' of the Zeme Naga tribe, perched on a steep hillside between Maram and Paren road in the Willong sub-division (about 135 km north of Imphal, about 85 km from Senapati HQ), with ancient war gates, the King's House and sacred bathing pools from the headhunting era; the state government has promised it 'heritage village' status. Coordinates are approximate (verify) — no published coordinates were found. CSV town 'Senapati' is the district, not the town.

name: Yangkhullen Village Church
town: Yangkhullen (CSV town 'Senapati' is the district; the village is in the Willong sub-division, Mao-Maram tehsil)
town_description: Yangkhullen (Ze Village) is a Zeme Naga 'hanging village' perched dramatically on a steep hillside between Maram and Paren road in Senapati district's Willong sub-division, adjoining Nagaland. Home to about 2,500 Zeme people, it preserves ancient war gates, stone fortifications, the King's House and sacred pools; most households are Christian (Baptist/Catholic) with a minority following the indigenous Paupai Renet/Heraka faith.
